name: Netherlands

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 18044027 inhabitants, recorded as 18.044 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Dutch, in the transversal venues pass. One unit, one house, against an opening estimate of 1.5 produced with no research. The Netherlands is named in this indicator's known_bias beside Italy and Spain as a system whose vitality runs through companies, and the pass confirms it without needing to argue: the country has a dense figure-theatre field and almost none of it holds a publicly backed hall. The Amstelveens Poppentheater, Wolfert van Borsselenweg 85A, has played for more than fifty years in a former kindergarten, holds 130 seats, and programmes puppet, object and visual theatre as a professional youth theatre; it is a stichting, and the gemeente Amstelveen granted it a guarantee subsidy of 42 000 euros alongside its other cultural institutions. A hall of its own, a puppetry programme, a municipality behind it. What is left out is the interesting part. Poppentheater Koos Kneus has its own room at Iepenplein 40 in Amsterdam-Oost, moved there in 2004 after seven years on the Commelinstraat, and plays every Sunday in two slots for two age groups — a diffusion venue by any reading, and it names no public funder anywhere on its pages, so it fails on backing and not on merit. The Ulrike Quade Company works from the Broedplaats De Vlugt in Amsterdam-West and Feikes Huis is a production platform; both are companies without a hall. Poppentheater Koekla from Edam plays some 150 performances a year in theatres, schools, community centres, libraries and festivals, which is a touring company and exactly what the denominator excludes. Theater De Krakeling in Amsterdam programmes puppetry among the genres of a youth theatre, which is a strand. One is what the denominator can prove and the upper bound is 3. The Nederlands Marionettentheater, which plays in the Zoldertheater in Amsterdam-Oost, and Poppentheater Diridas in Utrecht were not read for backing and either could raise it. The number should be read as a statement about how Dutch puppetry is housed. It is not a statement about how much of it there is, and in this country the gap between the two is at its widest.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained, and the exclusion here is more informative than the zero. The four Dutch higher theatre schools identified, ArtEZ Arnhem, AHK Amsterdam, Zuyd Maastricht and HKU Utrecht, show no puppetry stream: AHK's courses are acting and cabaret, mime, scenography, directing, design and technology, and production. The only specialised training identified is the Puppet and Object Theatre course at the Haags Theaterhuis in The Hague, which awards a certificate from the Dutch UNIMA puppetry association. The denominator excludes it: an association certificate is not a higher education award backed by a state institution. Method caveat: this description of the Haags Theaterhuis comes from a search summary, the page itself not having been readable. Confidence therefore stays at estimate. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1. This country is a textbook case of the bias flagged in the schema, where vitality runs through companies rather than institutions. Revisited on 2026-07-27 after the two rulings of the same day. Neither turns the file, but one sentence had to be restated. The Haags Theaterhuis was excluded because an association certificate is not a higher education award backed by a state institution, a formula that quotes a denominator which no longer exists. The exclusion survives its rewriting: the test is now that the award be state-recognised, and a certificate issued by the Dutch UNIMA association is not one, whoever owns the training. The object theatre ruling does not save it either, since what fails here is the award and not the discipline — the course is squarely puppet and object theatre. The method caveat stands untouched and is the real weakness of this file: the description of the Haags Theaterhuis still comes from a search summary, its own page never having been read, so nothing here is established at source about what it actually awards. Confidence stays at estimated for that reason and not for any other.
